QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_37

question.text: When determining sample size for an SIA engagement, Section 5.11.4 identifies which factors as relevant for statistically significant samples?

answer.text: Only the budget available for fieldwork

Type of universe (finite/infinite), sampling unit, sample size relative to time/cost/facility, sampling methodology informed by evaluation objectives; for statistical significance, define confidence interval and margin of error
A fixed 30-beneficiary sample applies regardless of universe size
SRO-prescribed minimum sample size of 10% of total beneficiaries in every engagement

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.11.4 'Determining Sample size' lists: Type of Universe (finite/infinite), Sampling Unit, Sample Size (dependent on time/cost/facility), and Sampling Methodology (depends on evaluation objectives, financial resources, time constraints, problem nature). For statistical significance, you must define confidence interval and margin of error. The Trap: A oversimplifies; C invents a uniform 30-sample rule; D invents a 10% SRO rule. None of these appear in the workbook. Cross-Exam Context: Research methodology in XV (RA) and XXIII share sampling theory; XXIII applies it to beneficiary counts, not market samples. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Document your confidence interval (usually 95%) and margin of error (5-10%) in the methodology annexure of the AIR — working backwards to justify a lower sample size post-hoc is a peer-review red flag.
